question: Does adding a governed software factory improve independently verified engineering delivery compared with the existing human-directed agent-assisted workflow under matched conditions?

arms.description: Existing human-directed, agent-assisted workflow with the same protected PR requirements
Candidate software-factory workflow with identical external verification and protected PR requirements

sampling.source: First eight eligible non-sensitive independently reviewed maintenance or defect-repair work orders admitted after this protocol is protected on main; independently lock actual task IDs, exact task base SHAs and oracle digests before arm allocation
exclusions: acceptance oracle supplied by a contestant before independent task admission
sampling.post_allocation_violation_policy: Retain every allocated task in its original arm and denominator even if the contestant tampers with tests or oracles; record FAILURE or UNKNOWN and stop affected execution for a safety/provenance violation; never admit a replacement
sampling.allocation: After freezing eight eligible distinct task IDs, their base SHAs and oracles, an independent evaluator generates a 32-byte seed as 64 lowercase hex characters. Rank task IDs by ascending SHA-256(UTF-8(seed + ':' + task_id)) raw digest, breaking any tie by task ID; allocate the first four distinct tasks to control, the remaining four to factory. Execute each task only once against the real protected repository; failures, non-starts and timeouts remain allocated and counted, with no replacements. The executable reference is tools/factory_evaluation_contract.py::allocation_schedule.

controls.balanced_interleaved_schedule: Use the allocation reference to strictly alternate four control and four factory task slots. Sort each arm by its already ranked SHA-256(UTF-8(seed + ':' + task_id)) digest, and choose the starting arm from the low bit of the last raw byte of SHA-256(UTF-8(seed + ':start')) (0=control, 1=factory); record chronological main SHA changes, and mark materially uncontrolled drift INCOMPARABLE.
controls.cross_arm_exposure_policy: Use separate fresh worker context and task workspaces; forbid sharing diagnoses, patches, prompts, private memory, review findings or generated artifacts across arms until all allocated tasks have terminal outcomes; independently record exposure and treat contaminated comparisons as INCOMPARABLE without removing allocated tasks
controls.human_intervention_definition: Any action by a human that changes task strategy, edits code, resolves an execution blocker, repairs evidence or manually advances an otherwise automated stage; initial task registration is excluded
controls.deviation_policy: Record actual variations before interpretation; materially unmatched versions, resources, or oracles make causal comparison INCOMPARABLE

execution_manifest.change_policy: Lock the independently reviewed complete implementation/configuration/agent prompt and tools manifest before executing the first task; no unregistered controller, model, prompt, tool, credential scope or adaptation changes mid-study; deviations require a new versioned cohort and retain old results

primary_metric.numerator: Eligible arm-task attempts with an independently confirmed correct change, exact-head substantive review, required checks, authorized protected merge and observed main ancestry within the budget
primary_metric.denominator: All eligible tasks assigned to that arm before execution, including timeout, non-start, blocked, failed and abandoned tasks
primary_metric.measurement_unit: verified deliveries per eligible allocated attempt

decision.success_condition: Report all randomized parallel-arm outcomes, task-class balance, protected-main drift and limitations without promoting a causal or general-reliability claim
decision.followup: Preregister confirmatory sample-size and statistical decision rule based on pilot uncertainty before subsequent testing

limitations: No factory control plane or coding worker is independently proven operational by this protocol.
Eight separately assigned tasks (four per arm) constitute a diagnostic pilot, not a powered superiority experiment; task-difficulty imbalance remains a material limitation.
Task IDs, credentials, actual runner parity, outcomes, provider cost and hosted provenance are not yet established.
An unmerged candidate protocol is not frozen authoritative evidence; freeze at the protected-main commit before trial allocation.
Passing a static validation tool does not authenticate source evidence or establish scientific acceptance.
